title: A New Way to Diagnose Obesity: Why Doctors Are Moving Beyond BMI
subtitle: A proposed diagnostic method could fix millions of incorrect health labels by looking at more than just weight and height.

summary.en: Doctors are proposing a new way to diagnose obesity that moves beyond the traditional Body Mass Index (BMI). Recent studies suggest that BMI often mislabels healthy people and misses those who truly need medical help. The new approach uses waist measurements and organ function tests to provide a more accurate picture of health. Experts believe this method will help doctors identify who is at risk of disease more effectively. This shift could change how millions of people receive medical care worldwide.
summary.zh: 醫師們正提出一種新的肥胖診斷方式，旨在超越傳統的身體質量指數（BMI）。近期研究顯示，身體質量指數經常誤標健康的人，並遺漏了真正需要醫療協助的病患。這種新方法利用腰圍測量與器官功能測試，以提供更準確的健康全貌。專家相信，此方法將有助於醫師更有效地辨識出誰有罹病風險。這項轉變可能會改變全球數百萬人接受醫療照護的方式。

paragraphs.en: For many years, doctors have used the Body Mass Index (BMI) to decide if someone is overweight or obese. BMI is a simple calculation that divides a person’s weight by their height. However, medical experts now say this tool is too simple and often gives the wrong results. According to The Guardian Health, a new approach is being proposed to fix these errors, which could prevent millions of people from being misdiagnosed.
paragraphs.zh: 多年來，醫師一直使用身體質量指數（BMI）來判定一個人是否過重或肥胖。身體質量指數是一項簡單的計算，將一個人的體重除以身高。然而，醫學專家現在表示，這種工具過於簡化，且經常得出錯誤的結果。根據《衛報健康》（The Guardian Health）報導，目前正提出一種新的方法來修正這些誤差，這可能防止數百萬人遭到誤診。

paragraphs.en: BMI has long been a standard tool in healthcare. It classifies people as overweight if their BMI is between 25 and 29.9, and obese if it is 30 or higher. Today, more than 70% of adults in the US and two-thirds of adults in the UK are labeled as overweight or obese using this system. However, experts argue that BMI is a 'blunt instrument'—a tool that is not sharp or precise enough for medical diagnosis. Because it only looks at weight and height, it fails to account for muscle mass, body fat distribution, or how well a person’s organs are working.
paragraphs.zh: 身體質量指數長期以來一直是醫療保健的標準工具。它將身體質量指數介於 25 到 29.9 之間的人歸類為過重，30 或以上則歸類為肥胖。如今，美國超過 70% 的成年人以及英國三分之二的成年人，都透過這套系統被標記為過重或肥胖。然而，專家認為身體質量指數是一種「鈍器」，也就是說，它對於醫療診斷而言不夠精確。由於它僅考量體重與身高，因此無法顧及肌肉量、體脂肪分佈，或是人體器官的運作狀況。

paragraphs.en: Professor Francisco Rubino of King’s College London explained that the inaccuracy of BMI is a major problem for both the healthcare system and individual patients. According to The Guardian Health, the new method suggests that BMI alone misses obesity in 5% to 9% of adults. At the same time, it wrongly labels up to 3% of people as having a health condition they do not actually have. By studying health records from over 800,000 people across the UK, US, China, and Spain, researchers found that combining BMI with other measurements provides a much clearer view of a patient’s health.
paragraphs.zh: 倫敦國王學院（King’s College London）的魯比諾教授（Professor Francisco Rubino）解釋說，身體質量指數的不準確性，對醫療體系與個別病患而言都是一個重大問題。根據《衛報健康》報導，新方法指出，單靠身體質量指數會遺漏 5% 到 9% 的肥胖成年人。同時，它也會錯誤地將多達 3% 的人標記為患有實際上並不存在的健康問題。透過研究英國、美國、中國與西班牙超過 80 萬人的健康紀錄，研究人員發現，將身體質量指數與其他測量數據結合，能提供更清晰的病患健康狀況。

paragraphs.en: This new diagnostic approach is more detailed than the old system. Under the new rules, doctors would still look at BMI, but they would also measure a patient’s waist. A high waist-to-height ratio or a large waist measurement—generally over 102cm for men and 88cm for women—would be a key sign of obesity. The process then goes a step further by separating patients into two categories: 'pre-clinical obesity' and 'clinical obesity.'
paragraphs.zh: 這種新的診斷方法比舊系統更為詳盡。在新規則下，醫師仍會參考身體質量指數，但也會測量病患的腰圍。腰圍身高比過高，或是腰圍過大（男性通常超過 102 公分，女性超過 88 公分），將成為肥胖的關鍵指標。該流程更進一步將病患分為兩類：「臨床前肥胖」與「臨床肥胖」。

paragraphs.en: Clinical obesity is defined as an active disease where excess body fat is already damaging how a person’s organs function. Pre-clinical obesity, on the other hand, means the extra fat is a health risk but has not yet caused serious problems. This distinction is vital. According to The Guardian Health, researchers found that 80% to 90% of people with pre-clinical obesity did not progress to the more dangerous, active disease over a 10-year period. This shows that not all people with a high BMI are in the same level of danger.
paragraphs.zh: 臨床肥胖被定義為一種活躍的疾病，即過多的體脂肪已經損害了人體器官的功能。另一方面，臨床前肥胖則意味著多餘的脂肪雖構成健康風險，但尚未造成嚴重問題。這種區別至關重要。根據《衛報健康》報導，研究人員發現，在 10 年期間內，80% 到 90% 的臨床前肥胖者並未惡化為更危險的活躍疾病。這顯示並非所有身體質量指數偏高的人，都處於相同程度的危險之中。

paragraphs.en: This change could have a significant impact on how doctors treat their patients. For example, three different people might all have a BMI of 32. Under the old system, all three would be labeled as obese. With the new method, one person might be found to have no excess body fat and be considered healthy. A second person might have extra fat but no organ damage, while the third might have both excess fat and organ dysfunction. By identifying these differences, doctors can provide care that is better suited to each person’s specific needs.
paragraphs.zh: 這項改變可能會對醫師治療病患的方式產生重大影響。例如，三個人可能都擁有 32 的身體質量指數。在舊系統下，這三人全都會被標記為肥胖。但在新方法下，其中一人可能被發現並無過多體脂肪而被視為健康。第二個人可能有多餘脂肪但無器官損傷，而第三個人則可能同時有脂肪過多與器官功能障礙。透過辨識這些差異，醫師能提供更適合每個人特定需求的照護。

paragraphs.en: While this new method is more complex for doctors to use, experts believe it is a necessary step forward. The goal is to ensure that healthcare is based on a person’s actual health status rather than just a simple number. As the medical community continues to discuss these changes, the focus remains on improving accuracy to ensure that patients receive the right treatment at the right time. By moving beyond the limits of BMI, doctors hope to better identify who is truly at risk and who can be reassured about their health.
paragraphs.zh: 雖然這種新方法對醫師而言操作較為複雜，但專家認為這是必要的前進步驟。其目標是確保醫療保健是基於個人的實際健康狀況，而非僅僅是一個簡單的數字。隨著醫學界持續討論這些變革，重點仍放在提升準確性，以確保病患能在正確的時間獲得正確的治療。透過超越身體質量指數的限制，醫師希望能更有效地辨識出誰真正處於風險之中，以及誰可以對自己的健康感到放心。

keyTerms.definitionEn: A tool or method that is not precise or subtle enough for a specific task.
keyTerms.definitionZh: 比喻不夠精確、粗糙的工具或方法。
keyTerms.noteZh: 字面意思是「鈍器」，這裡用來比喻 BMI 測量方式過於粗略。文中：However, experts argue that BMI is a 'blunt instrument'—a tool that is not sharp or precise enough for medical diagnosis.

keyTerms.definitionEn: To consider or include something when making a decision or judgment.
keyTerms.noteZh: 常見於「解釋原因」，這裡指在診斷時將特定因素納入考量。文中：Because it only looks at weight and height, it fails to account for muscle mass, body fat distribution, or how well a person’s organs are working.

keyTerms.definitionEn: To develop or move forward to a more advanced or serious stage.
keyTerms.noteZh: 常見作名詞（進步），這裡作動詞，指病情惡化到更嚴重的階段。文中：According to The Guardian Health, researchers found that 80% to 90% of people with pre-clinical obesity did not progress to the more dangerous, active disease over a 10-year period.

previousArticles.summaryEn: Doctors are looking for better ways to identify obesity beyond the traditional Body Mass Index (BMI). A new study shows that BMI often misdiagnoses millions of people worldwide. The proposed method uses waist measurements and organ function tests to get a clearer picture of health. Experts believe this approach will help doctors treat patients more accurately. While the new process is more complex, it could lead to better long-term health outcomes.

quiz.question: According to the research mentioned in the article, what is the primary reason the new diagnostic method is considered more accurate than BMI alone?

options.A: It ignores BMI entirely and focuses only on waist measurements.
options.B: It combines BMI with other physical measurements to assess health.
options.C: It identifies that 90% of people with high BMI are actually healthy.
options.D: It relies on a 10-year study that proves BMI is completely useless.

quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案為 B。文章第三段明確指出，研究人員發現將 BMI 與其他測量數據（如腰圍）結合，能提供更清晰的健康視角。選項 A 錯誤，因為新方法仍會參考 BMI；選項 C 錯誤，因為文章提到的是 80% 到 90% 的「臨床前肥胖」者未惡化，而非所有 BMI 高者；選項 D 過度誇大，文章僅稱 BMI 為「遲鈍的工具」，並未說其完全無用。

quiz.question: Based on the article, what can be inferred about a person who is categorized as having 'pre-clinical obesity'?

options.A: They are guaranteed to develop serious organ damage within ten years.
options.B: They currently have no excess body fat but are at risk of gaining it.
options.C: They possess health risks due to body fat but do not yet suffer from active organ damage.
options.D: They require immediate medical intervention to prevent death.

quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案為 C。根據第五段，臨床前肥胖（pre-clinical obesity）定義為脂肪雖構成健康風險，但尚未造成嚴重的器官功能損害。選項 A 與文章中提到「80% 到 90% 的人未惡化」矛盾；選項 B 錯誤，因為該類別正是因為有「多餘脂肪」才被標記；選項 D 過於武斷，文中並未要求所有人必須立即進行醫療介入。

quiz.question: In the second paragraph, the author describes BMI as a 'blunt instrument.' What does 'blunt' mean in this context?

options.A: Lacking the precision or sharpness needed for fine tasks.
options.B: Physically heavy and difficult to move or handle.
options.C: Extremely direct and honest in a way that hurts feelings.
options.D: Very powerful and effective at hitting a target.

quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案為 A。在此上下文中，「blunt instrument」意指該工具不夠精確（not sharp or precise enough），無法區分肌肉量或脂肪分佈。選項 B 與物理重量無關；選項 C 是「直言不諱」的意思，不符合醫療工具的語境；選項 D 與原文描述 BMI 容易出錯的觀點完全相反。

quiz.question: What is the central message of the article?

options.A: BMI should be banned because it is an outdated and harmful measurement.
options.B: Doctors need to stop using numbers and rely only on visual observation.
options.C: The medical community is transitioning to a more nuanced, multi-factor approach to diagnosing obesity.
options.D: Weight is the most important factor in determining whether a patient is healthy.

quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案為 C。文章核心在於說明 BMI 的侷限性，並介紹了一種結合腰圍與區分肥胖程度的新方法，旨在提供更精確的診斷。選項 A 過於極端，文章僅建議改進而非全面禁用；選項 B 錯誤，因為新方法仍包含具體的測量數據；選項 D 與文章主旨背道而馳，文章正是強調不能僅依賴體重。
